metadata.name: Regulation on Personal Data Transfer Outside the Kingdom
metadata.description: The SDAIA Regulation on Personal Data Transfer Outside the Kingdom implements Article (29) of the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree No. M/19 dated 9/2/1443 AH) and its amendments. It establishes the permissible purposes, appropriate safeguards, exemptions, adequacy-evaluation mechanism, subsequent-transfer rules, exemption-revocation conditions, and risk-assessment obligations governing the transfer or disclosure of personal data by controllers to any party outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
metadata.classification_reasoning: This is a binding implementing regulation issued by SDAIA, the competent authority under the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree No. M/19). It imposes mandatory obligations ('shall', 'must') on controllers transferring or disclosing personal data outside the Kingdom, including implementation of appropriate safeguards, risk assessments, and recordkeeping, and is enforceable upon publication in the Official Gazette. Version 2.0 came into force on 1 September 2024, ahead of full PDPL enforcement on 14 September 2024.
metadata.framework_purpose: To regulate and safeguard the transfer or disclosure of personal data by controllers to parties outside the Kingdom, ensuring that such data continues to enjoy an appropriate level of protection not less than that prescribed by the Personal Data Protection Law and its Regulations, while operationalizing Article (29) of the Law.
metadata.framework_scope: All controllers subject to the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law that transfer or disclose personal data to any party (entity, country, or international organization) outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including subsequent (onward) transfers, and including destinations evaluated at the level of cities, special economic zones, and global trade centers.
framework_objectives: Define additional permissible purposes for transferring or disclosing personal data outside the Kingdom under Article 29(1)(d) of the Law
Establish the mechanism, criteria, and review cycle for evaluating the adequacy of personal data protection in destination countries and international organizations
Empower the competent authority to publish, amend, and suspend the adequacy list and to extend adequacy standards to cities, special economic zones, and global trade centers
Define the appropriate safeguards (standard contractual clauses, binding common rules, certificate of accreditation) controllers must implement
Specify the exemption cases from the two transfer conditions under Article 29(2)(b) and (c) of the Law and the safeguards applicable to each
Ensure appropriate safeguards protect data subject rights, including the right to complaint and compensation
Apply the Law and Regulations to subsequent (onward) transfers of personal data
Set the conditions and consequences for revocation of exemptions, including halting transfers and notifying recipients
Mandate risk assessments before transferring or disclosing personal data outside the Kingdom in defined cases and prescribe the elements of such assessments
Require the competent authority to issue guides and guidelines supplementing the Regulation
metadata.target_audience: Controllers (public and private entities subject to the KSA PDPL), Data Protection Officers (DPOs), Legal & Compliance functions, Privacy/Data Governance teams, and processors involved in cross-border personal data transfers from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
metadata.regulatory_authority: Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA) — the competent authority under the Personal Data Protection Law issued pursuant to Royal Decree No. (M/19) dated 9/2/1443 AH and its amendments
metadata.penalty_for_non_compliance: Penalties are not specified within this Regulation; violations are subject to the enforcement and penalty provisions of the Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree No. M/19) and its Implementing Regulations, which include warnings and financial penalties and, for certain violations involving the unlawful transfer or disclosure of sensitive data outside the Kingdom, criminal penalties. The competent authority may also revoke exemptions and suspend transfers.
metadata.adoption_approach: Risk-based and safeguard-based implementation. Controllers must rely on the competent authority's adequacy list or, where exempted from the transfer conditions, implement appropriate safeguards (standard contractual clauses, binding common rules, or a certificate of accreditation), conduct risk assessments in defined cases, maintain records, and halt transfers where exemptions are revoked.

sections: Article 2: Other Purposes for Transferring or Disclosing Personal Data to Entities Outside the Kingdom
Article 3: Procedures and Standards for Evaluating the Level of Personal Data Protection Outside the Kingdom
Article 4: Cases in Which Controllers Are Exempt from the Requirements to Comply with the Appropriate Level of Protection and the Minimum Transfer of Personal Data
Article 5: Subsequent Transfer of Personal Data
Article 7: Risk Assessment of Transferring or Disclosing Personal Data to a Party Outside the Kingdom

controls.title: Other Permissible Purposes for Transfer or Disclosure Outside the Kingdom
controls.description: Transfers or disclosures of personal data outside the Kingdom for other purposes must comply with Article 29(1)(d) of the Law, including central processing operations, providing a service or benefit to the data subject, and conducting scientific research and studies.
controls.full_text: Other purposes for transferring or disclosing personal data to a party outside the Kingdom shall comply with subparagraph (d) of paragraph (1) of Article (29) of the Law, including: 1. Performing necessary operations for central processing to enable the controller to conduct its activities. 2. To provide a service or benefit to the subject of the personal data. 3. Conducting scientific research and studies.

evidence_requirements.name: Cross-Border Transfer Purpose Register
evidence_requirements.description: Register mapping every transfer or disclosure of personal data outside the Kingdom to a permitted purpose under Article 29(1)(d) — central processing operations, service/benefit to the data subject, or scientific research — with legal basis and approver.

evidence_requirements.name: Legal Basis Assessment
evidence_requirements.description: Documented legal basis assessment tying each cross-border transfer to subparagraph (d) of paragraph (1) of Article (29) and the specific permissible purpose relied upon.

evidence_requirements.name: Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) — Cross-Border Extract
evidence_requirements.description: Extract from the RoPA evidencing the transfer purpose, recipient, destination and category of data for each outbound transfer.

evidence_requirements.name: Central Processing Necessity Memo
evidence_requirements.description: Memo justifying that the transfer is necessary for central processing operations enabling the controller to conduct its activities (where this purpose is relied upon).

controls.title: Adequacy List Publication, Four-Year Review, and Evaluation Criteria
controls.description: The competent authority publishes on its official website a list of countries/international organizations providing an appropriate level of protection and reviews it every four years (or as necessary) against six criteria covering protective regulations, a supervisory body, cooperation readiness, non-conflicting disclosure requirements, treaty obligations, and onward-transfer provisions.
controls.full_text: The competent authority shall publish on its official website a list of countries or international organizations that provide an appropriate level of protection for personal data not less than that prescribed by the Law and Regulations. The competent authority shall review this list every four years, or as necessary, based on the following criteria: A. The existence of regulations that ensure the protection of personal data and the rights of data subjects, including the right to seek compensation for damages caused by violations of these rights. These regulations must meet at least the level of protection prescribed by Law and Regulations. B. The existence of a supervisory body responsible for enforcing the provisions related to the protection of personal data. C. The supervisory authority is prepared to cooperate with the competent authority in the Kingdom on matters related to the protection of personal data. D. The regulatory requirements related to the disclosure of personal data under the relevant statutory provisions applicable in the State or international organization must not conflict with the provisions for the disclosure of personal data set forth in the Law and Regulations, nor with any other statutory provisions in force in the Kingdom. E. Obligations arising from international treaties or agreements binding on a State or an international organization, as well as those related to its membership in regional or multilateral organizations, which may require the transfer of personal data. F. Provisions related to subsequent transfers of personal data, as stipulated in Article (5) of the Regulation.

evidence_requirements.name: Adequacy List Verification Record
evidence_requirements.description: Dated record / screenshot confirming the destination country or international organization appeared on the competent authority's published list of jurisdictions providing an appropriate level of protection at the time of each transfer relying on the adequacy route.

evidence_requirements.name: Destination Adequacy Register
evidence_requirements.description: Internal register of transfer destinations with their adequacy status, source reference to the published list, and the four-year re-verification cycle.

evidence_requirements.name: Adequacy Criteria Mapping
evidence_requirements.description: Where the controller performs supporting due diligence, a mapping of the destination jurisdiction against criteria A–F (protective regulations, supervisory body, cooperation readiness, non-conflicting disclosure requirements, treaty obligations, subsequent-transfer provisions).

evidence_requirements.name: Periodic Adequacy Re-check Log
evidence_requirements.description: Log of periodic re-verification of destinations against the competent authority's list, aligned with the authority's four-year (or as-necessary) review cycle.

controls.title: Amendment of the Adequacy List
controls.description: The competent authority may amend the adequacy list per statutory procedures, and where a review indicates a listed country/organization no longer guarantees an appropriate level of protection, it may engage the relevant authorities to address the reasons for exclusion.
controls.full_text: The competent authority may amend the list of countries or international organizations that ensure an appropriate level of protection for personal data transferred outside the Kingdom not less than that prescribed by the Law and Regulations in accordance with the statutory procedures. If a review indicates that any of these countries or organizations no longer guarantees an appropriate level of protection, the competent authority may work with the relevant authorities in the State or the international organization to address the reasons for its exclusion from the list.

evidence_requirements.name: Adequacy List Change Monitoring Log
evidence_requirements.description: Log evidencing ongoing monitoring of additions, amendments, and removals to the competent authority's adequacy list, with detection dates and source.

evidence_requirements.name: List-Change Impact Assessment
evidence_requirements.description: Assessment of the impact on existing transfers when a destination is added to or removed from the adequacy list, including remediation actions where adequacy is lost.

controls.title: Suspension of Transfers to Listed Countries or Organizations
controls.description: The competent authority may suspend the transfer or disclosure of personal data to any country or organization listed under paragraph (1), in accordance with statutory procedures.
controls.full_text: The competent authority may suspend the transfer or disclosure of personal data to any of the countries or organizations listed in paragraph (1) of this Article, in accordance with the statutory procedures.

evidence_requirements.name: Transfer Suspension Response Procedure
evidence_requirements.description: Documented procedure to identify, halt, and contain transfers to a country or organization whose transfers have been suspended by the competent authority.

evidence_requirements.name: Suspension Notification Handling Log
evidence_requirements.description: Log of any suspension notices received from the competent authority, the affected transfers, and the actions taken in response.

controls.title: Application of Adequacy Standards to Cities, Special Economic Zones, and Global Trade Centers
controls.description: The standards applied to countries and international organizations for evaluating the level of personal data protection outside the Kingdom also apply to cities, special economic zones, and global trade centers.
controls.full_text: The standards applied to countries and international organizations for evaluating the level of protection of personal data outside the Kingdom shall also apply to cities, special economic zones, and global trade centers.

evidence_requirements.name: Sub-Jurisdiction Adequacy Assessment
evidence_requirements.description: Assessment confirming that destinations at the level of cities, special economic zones, and global trade centers are evaluated against the same adequacy standards applied to countries and international organizations.

evidence_requirements.name: Destination Granularity Register
evidence_requirements.description: Register capturing the precise destination of data including city, special economic zone, or global trade center where relevant, with adequacy status.

controls.title: Appropriate Safeguards to be Implemented in Exemption Cases
controls.description: In the exemption cases under paragraph (2), the controller shall implement appropriate safeguards: standard contractual clauses, binding common rules, or a certificate of accreditation.
controls.full_text: In accordance with the cases of exemption specified in paragraph (2) of this Article, the controller shall implement the following appropriate safeguards: A. Standard contractual clauses. B. Binding common rules. C. Certificate of accreditation.

evidence_requirements.name: Appropriate Safeguards Selection Record
evidence_requirements.description: Documented selection, per exempt transfer, of the appropriate safeguard implemented — standard contractual clauses, binding common rules, or certificate of accreditation — with rationale.

evidence_requirements.name: Executed Standard Contractual Clauses
evidence_requirements.description: Signed standard contractual clauses in the standard form issued by the competent authority for the relevant transfers.

evidence_requirements.name: Approved Binding Common Rules
evidence_requirements.description: Binding common rules adopted by the controller and applicable across the multinational group, ensuring protection not less than that prescribed by the Law and Regulations.

evidence_requirements.name: Certificate of Accreditation
evidence_requirements.description: Certificate of accreditation obtained from an entity licensed by the competent authority where relied upon as the appropriate safeguard.

evidence_requirements.name: Safeguards Implementation Register
evidence_requirements.description: Register mapping each exempt cross-border transfer to the safeguard implemented, its status, and validity dates.

controls.title: Exemption from the Two Transfer Conditions — General Rule
controls.description: The controller is exempt from the two conditions under Article 29(2)(b) and (c) of the Law (or either of them), but transfers/disclosures outside the Kingdom remain subject to appropriate safeguards in the cases enumerated in subparagraphs A–E.
controls.full_text: The controller is exempt from the two conditions required for transferring or disclosing personal data to a party outside the Kingdom, as stipulated in paragraphs (b) and (c) of paragraph (2) of Article (29) of the Law, or either of them. However, the transfer or disclosure of personal data to a party outside the Kingdom shall still be subject to appropriate safeguards in the following cases:

evidence_requirements.name: Exemption Eligibility Assessment
evidence_requirements.description: Assessment confirming the transfer qualifies for exemption from the two conditions under Article 29(2)(b) and/or (c) of the Law and identifying which of the cases (A–E) applies.

evidence_requirements.name: Appropriate Safeguards Evidence
evidence_requirements.description: Evidence that appropriate safeguards remain in place for the transfer notwithstanding the exemption from the two conditions.

evidence_requirements.name: Transfer Conditions Exemption Register
evidence_requirements.description: Register recording each exempt transfer, the condition(s) exempted, the applicable case, and the safeguard applied.

controls.title: Exemption Case — Transfers Between Public Bodies Under a Kingdom Agreement
controls.description: Where transfer/disclosure is between public bodies to implement an agreement to which the Kingdom is a party or to serve its interests, controllers must include standard provisions for personal data protection in the relevant agreements or memoranda of understanding.
controls.full_text: If the transfer or disclosure of personal data is to be made between public bodies to implement an agreement to which the Kingdom is a party or to serve its interests, the controllers must include standard provisions for the protection of personal data in the relevant agreements or memoranda of understanding.

evidence_requirements.name: Inter-Governmental Agreement / MoU with Data Protection Provisions
evidence_requirements.description: The executed agreement or memorandum of understanding implementing the Kingdom's agreement, containing standard provisions for the protection of personal data.

evidence_requirements.name: Standard Data Protection Provisions Mapping
evidence_requirements.description: Mapping confirming the required standard personal data protection provisions are present in each relevant agreement or MoU.

evidence_requirements.name: Public Body Transfer Authorization
evidence_requirements.description: Authorization/approval record confirming the public-body-to-public-body transfer is to implement an agreement to which the Kingdom is a party or to serve its interests.

controls.title: Exemption Case — Non-Recurring or Limited Transfers
controls.description: Where the transfer/disclosure is non-recurring or for a limited period and involves a limited number of data subjects, the controller must comply with standard contractual clauses; alternatively, the transfer may be made to a body holding an approval certificate from a licensed entity provided the data is not sensitive.
controls.full_text: If the transfer or disclosure is non-recurring or for a limited period and involves a limited number of data subjects, the controller must comply with the standard contractual clauses. Alternatively, if the transfer or disclosure is made to a body that has received an approval certificate from an entity licensed by the competent authority and the data is not sensitive.

evidence_requirements.name: Executed Standard Contractual Clauses
evidence_requirements.description: Signed standard contractual clauses governing the non-recurring or limited-period transfer.

evidence_requirements.name: Non-Recurring / Limited Transfer Justification
evidence_requirements.description: Documentation evidencing that the transfer is non-recurring or for a limited period and involves a limited number of data subjects.

evidence_requirements.name: Recipient Approval Certificate
evidence_requirements.description: Approval certificate held by the recipient body, issued by an entity licensed by the competent authority, where the alternative route is relied upon.

evidence_requirements.name: Sensitivity Screening Record
evidence_requirements.description: Record confirming the data is not sensitive when relying on the approval-certificate alternative.

controls.title: Exemption Case — Central Operations Within a Multinational Group
controls.description: Where the transfer is necessary to perform central operations and the controller is part of a group of multinational entities, the controller and its affiliates must comply with binding common rules or standard contractual clauses; alternatively, the recipient must obtain a certificate of approval from a licensed body.
controls.full_text: If the transfer or disclosure of personal data is necessary to perform central operations and the controller is part of a group of multinational entities, the controller and its affiliates must comply with binding common rules or standard contractual clauses that ensure adherence to the requirements stipulated by the Law and Regulations. Alternatively, the entity to which the personal data will be transferred or disclosed must obtain a certificate of approval issued by a body licensed by the competent authority.

evidence_requirements.name: Binding Common Rules or Executed SCCs
evidence_requirements.description: Approved binding common rules applicable to the controller and its affiliates, or executed standard contractual clauses, ensuring adherence to the Law and Regulations.

evidence_requirements.name: Multinational Group & Central Operations Memo
evidence_requirements.description: Memo evidencing that the controller is part of a group of multinational entities and that the transfer is necessary to perform central operations.

evidence_requirements.name: Recipient Certificate of Approval
evidence_requirements.description: Certificate of approval obtained by the recipient entity from a body licensed by the competent authority, where the alternative route is relied upon.

evidence_requirements.name: Intra-Group Data Transfer Agreement
evidence_requirements.description: Intra-group data transfer agreement governing the central-operations transfer among the multinational entities.

controls.title: Exemption Case — Service or Benefit Directly to the Data Subject
controls.description: Where the transfer/disclosure is made to provide a service or benefit directly to the data subject without violating their expectations or interests, it must be to a party holding an approval certificate from a licensed body, provided the data is not sensitive.
controls.full_text: If the transfer or disclosure is made to provide a service or benefit directly to the data subject in a manner that does not violate their expectations or conflict with their interests, and if the transfer or disclosure is to a party that has received an approval certificate from a body licensed by the competent authority, provided that the data must not be sensitive.

evidence_requirements.name: Recipient Approval Certificate
evidence_requirements.description: Approval certificate held by the recipient party, issued by a body licensed by the competent authority.

evidence_requirements.name: Service/Benefit & Data Subject Expectations Assessment
evidence_requirements.description: Assessment evidencing the transfer provides a service or benefit directly to the data subject in a manner that does not violate their expectations or conflict with their interests.

evidence_requirements.name: Sensitivity Screening Record
evidence_requirements.description: Record confirming the data transferred is not sensitive.

controls.title: Exemption Case — Scientific Research and Studies
controls.description: Where the transfer/disclosure is necessary for scientific research and studies, it must be limited to the minimum data required and the controller must comply with standard contractual clauses or ensure the recipient holds an approval certificate from a licensed entity, provided the data is not sensitive.
controls.full_text: If the transfer or disclosure of personal data is necessary for conducting scientific research and studies, it must be limited to the minimum amount of data required. The controller must either comply with standard contractual clauses or ensure that the transfer or disclosure is made to a body that has received an approval certificate from an entity licensed by the competent authority, provided that the data must not be sensitive.

evidence_requirements.name: Data Minimization Record
evidence_requirements.description: Record evidencing that the transfer for scientific research is limited to the minimum amount of data required to achieve the research purpose.

evidence_requirements.name: Executed SCCs or Recipient Approval Certificate
evidence_requirements.description: Executed standard contractual clauses, or the recipient body's approval certificate from an entity licensed by the competent authority.

evidence_requirements.name: Research Purpose & Non-Sensitivity Assessment
evidence_requirements.description: Assessment documenting the scientific research purpose and confirming the data is not sensitive.

controls.title: Safeguards Must Ensure Compliance and Protect Data Subject Rights
controls.description: Appropriate safeguards must ensure controllers comply with the Law and Regulations and protect data subject rights, including the right to file a complaint with the competent authority and to seek compensation for damage from rights violations.
controls.full_text: Appropriate safeguards must ensure that controllers comply with the provisions set out in the Law and its Regulations, as well as protect the rights of personal data subjects, including the right to file a complaint with the competent authority and to seek compensation for any damage caused by violations of these rights.

evidence_requirements.name: Data Subject Rights Procedure
evidence_requirements.description: Procedure ensuring data subject rights are upheld in cross-border transfers, including the right to complaint to the competent authority and the right to seek compensation for damage from rights violations.

evidence_requirements.name: Safeguards Adequacy Assessment
evidence_requirements.description: Assessment demonstrating the implemented safeguards ensure compliance with the Law and Regulations and protect data subject rights.

evidence_requirements.name: Complaint Handling Mechanism Evidence
evidence_requirements.description: Evidence of an operational complaint-handling mechanism and a log of complaints relating to cross-border transfers and their resolution.

controls.title: Periodic Review of Safeguard Adequacy by the Competent Authority
controls.description: The competent authority may review the adequacy of the appropriate safeguards specified for each exemption case and may amend them every two years or as necessary.
controls.full_text: The competent authority may review the adequacy of the appropriate safeguards specified for each exemption case outlined in paragraph (2) of this Article, and may amend them every two years or as necessary.

evidence_requirements.name: Safeguards Re-Assessment Schedule
evidence_requirements.description: Controller's schedule for periodic re-assessment of implemented safeguards, aligned to the competent authority's biennial (or as-necessary) review and amendment cycle.

evidence_requirements.name: Updated Safeguards Documentation
evidence_requirements.description: Records of safeguard updates made in response to amendments to the appropriate safeguards by the competent authority.

controls.title: Application of the Law and Regulations to Subsequent Transfers
controls.description: Without prejudice to Articles (8) and (15) of the Law and Article (17) of the Implementing Regulations, the Law and Regulations apply to subsequent (onward) transfers of personal data that has been transferred or disclosed outside the Kingdom.
controls.full_text: Without prejudice to the provisions of Articles (8) and (15) of the Law and Article (17) of the Implementing Regulations, the Law and Regulations shall apply to subsequent transfers of personal data that has been transferred or disclosed to a party outside the Kingdom.

evidence_requirements.name: Onward Transfer Control Clauses
evidence_requirements.description: Standard contractual clauses / contractual provisions extending compliance with the Law and Regulations to any subsequent (onward) transfer by the recipient.

evidence_requirements.name: Subsequent Transfer Register
evidence_requirements.description: Register tracking onward transfers performed by recipients of data transferred outside the Kingdom, with destinations and safeguards.

evidence_requirements.name: Onward Transfer Compliance Attestation
evidence_requirements.description: Recipient attestation confirming that any subsequent transfer will comply with the Law and Regulations.

controls.title: Conditions Triggering Revocation of Exemption
controls.description: Exemptions granted under Article (4) do not apply where the controller fails to implement the appropriate safeguards, or where the competent authority determines the safeguards are inadequate for a specific case.
controls.full_text: None of the exemptions granted in accordance with the cases stipulated in Article (4) of the Regulation shall apply if any of the following situations arise: A. The controller has failed to implement the appropriate safeguards. B. If the competent authority determines that the appropriate safeguards are inadequate for any specific case.

evidence_requirements.name: Safeguards Implementation Monitoring Log
evidence_requirements.description: Log monitoring the continued implementation and operating effectiveness of appropriate safeguards for each exempt transfer.

evidence_requirements.name: Exemption Validity Review Records
evidence_requirements.description: Periodic review records confirming that safeguards remain implemented and adequate, so that the exemption continues to apply.

evidence_requirements.name: Competent Authority Determination Handling Procedure
evidence_requirements.description: Procedure for handling a determination by the competent authority that safeguards are inadequate for a specific case, including consequent loss of exemption.

controls.title: Halt Transfer and Notify Recipients on Loss of Exemption
controls.description: If either revocation condition in paragraph (1) is met, the controller shall halt the transfer or disclosure and notify the entities to whom the personal data was transferred or disclosed.
controls.full_text: If any of the conditions stipulated in subparagraphs (a) and (b) of paragraph (1) of this Article are met, the controller shall halt the transfer or disclosure and notify the entities to whom the personal data was transferred or disclosed.

evidence_requirements.name: Transfer Halt Procedure
evidence_requirements.description: Documented procedure to promptly halt the transfer or disclosure of personal data when an exemption is revoked under Article 6(1).

evidence_requirements.name: Recipient Notification Records
evidence_requirements.description: Records of notifications sent to the entities to whom the personal data was transferred or disclosed upon halting the transfer.

evidence_requirements.name: Cessation & Notification Log
evidence_requirements.description: Log recording each halted transfer, the triggering condition, the halt date, and the recipients notified.

controls.title: Mandatory Risk Assessment Before Transfer — Triggering Cases
controls.description: The controller shall conduct a risk assessment before transferring or disclosing personal data outside the Kingdom when relying on Article (4) of the Regulation, or when transferring/disclosing sensitive data outside the Kingdom on a continuous or widespread basis.
controls.full_text: The controller shall conduct a risk assessment before transferring or disclosing personal data to a party outside the Kingdom in the following cases: A. Transfer or disclosure of personal data to a party outside the Kingdom in accordance with Article (4) of the Regulation. B. Transferring or disclosing sensitive data to entities outside the Kingdom on a continuous or widespread basis.

evidence_requirements.name: Risk Assessment Trigger Register
evidence_requirements.description: Register logging when a transfer risk assessment is required — transfers under Article (4) and continuous/widespread transfers of sensitive data — with the assessment reference for each.

evidence_requirements.name: Completed Pre-Transfer Risk Assessments
evidence_requirements.description: Completed risk assessments evidenced to have been performed before the transfer or disclosure took place.

evidence_requirements.name: Sensitive Data Transfer Inventory
evidence_requirements.description: Inventory identifying transfers of sensitive data to entities outside the Kingdom carried out on a continuous or widespread basis.

controls.title: Required Elements of the Transfer Risk Assessment
controls.description: The transfer risk assessment should include: purpose and legal basis; nature and geographical scope of the transfer; adequacy of safeguards; data-minimization measures (where not exempted by Article 29(2)(c)); potential material/moral effects and likelihood; and measures or controls to prevent or mitigate risks.
controls.full_text: Risk assessment of transferring or disclosing personal data to a party outside the Kingdom should include the following elements: A. The purpose and legal basis for transferring or disclosing personal data to a party outside the Kingdom. B. A description of the nature of the transfer or disclosure of personal data to a party outside the Kingdom, including the activities involved in processing the data and their geographical scope. C. The appropriate safeguards and measures implemented for transferring or disclosing personal data to a party outside the Kingdom, and their adequacy in ensuring an appropriate level of protection for personal data not less than that prescribed by the Law and Regulations. D. The measures used to ensure that the transfer or disclosure of personal data to a party outside the Kingdom is limited to the minimum amount of data required to achieve the intended purposes, in cases not exempted by subparagraph (c) of paragraph (2) of Article (29) of the Law. E. The potential material or moral effects of transferring or disclosing personal data to a party outside the Kingdom and the likelihood of their occurrence. F. The measures or controls that will be applied to prevent potential risks to personal data subjects or to mitigate their effects if they occur.

evidence_requirements.name: Transfer Risk Assessment Report
evidence_requirements.description: Completed transfer risk assessment report covering all six elements (A–F): purpose and legal basis; nature and geographical scope; safeguards and their adequacy; data minimization; potential material/moral effects and likelihood; and preventive/mitigating measures.

evidence_requirements.name: Transfer Risk Assessment Template
evidence_requirements.description: Standard template enumerating the required elements A–F to ensure consistent and complete assessments.

evidence_requirements.name: Risk Treatment / Mitigation Plan
evidence_requirements.description: Plan documenting the measures or controls applied to prevent or mitigate identified risks to data subjects, with owners and status.

evidence_requirements.name: Element Coverage Matrix
evidence_requirements.description: Matrix confirming each required element (A–F) is addressed within each completed transfer risk assessment.

controls.title: Issuance of Guides and Guidelines by the Competent Authority
controls.description: The competent authority shall issue guides and guidelines related to the provisions contained in this Regulation.
controls.full_text: The competent authority shall issue guides and guidelines related to the provisions contained in this regulation.

evidence_requirements.name: SDAIA Guidance Monitoring Register
evidence_requirements.description: Register tracking guides and guidelines issued by the competent authority that relate to this Regulation (e.g., the Risk Assessment Guideline, Standard Contractual Clauses), with applicability assessment.

evidence_requirements.name: Guidance Implementation Records
evidence_requirements.description: Records demonstrating that issued guides and guidelines have been reviewed and reflected in the controller's transfer processes and documentation.

controls.title: Enforcement — Entry into Force
controls.description: The Regulation enters into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.
controls.full_text: The Regulation shall enter into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

evidence_requirements.name: Compliance Readiness Record
evidence_requirements.description: Record confirming awareness of the Regulation's entry into force upon Official Gazette publication and the controller's compliance go-live for cross-border transfers.

evidence_requirements.name: Official Gazette Publication Reference
evidence_requirements.description: Reference to the Official Gazette publication establishing the effective date of the Regulation.
